fields.value: Admission Committee for Professional Post-Graduate Medical Educational Courses (ACPPGMEC), Government of Gujarat, Gandhinagar
In-service doctor of the Government of Gujarat (needs NOC from a Gujarat competent authority)
NRI quota (NQ) seats, allotted on inter-se merit among candidates who applied for NRI seats.

Buy the registration PIN on medadmgujarat.org for ₹28,000: ₹3,000 non-refundable registration fee plus a ₹25,000 refundable security deposit. The E-PIN is sent to your mobile by SMS. If your number is registered with DND, you may not receive it.

Enter the PIN serial number, 14-digit PIN, email, mobile and NEET roll number. Fill in your details, set an alphanumeric password of 6–12 characters, and confirm with the OTP sent to your mobile. Then upload documents as PDF, JPG, JPEG or PNG. By submitting, you declare your details are true, agree to pay the fees fixed by the Fee Regulatory Committee, accept that ragging is punishable and that the committee's decision is final, and acknowledge that hiding or distorting information makes your admission liable to cancellation. After you click Confirm, you can only change details at the help centre, before verification.
Booking an appointment in advance is compulsory. When you print your registration slip, pick the date, time and help centre for document verification.
Verify documents at the help centre

Bring the printed registration details signed by you and a parent or guardian, all originals and one self-attested photocopy set. The officer stamps your registration slip. Without it you can't continue in the admission process.
NRI applicants: verify at the ACPPGMEC office

For NRI candidates, document verification and submission is done only at the office of ACPPGMEC, GMERS Medical College, Gandhinagar, where you also hand in the ₹25,000 processing-fee demand draft. The NRI instructions also mention booking a help-centre appointment, so confirm the arrangement with ACPPGMEC.
ACPPGMEC publishes the merit list of eligible candidates. Check your merit number and category against your registration details.
Fill choices and get your allotment
Choice filling opens online for each round. After it closes, allotments are published and you can see yours by logging in.
Pay the tuition fee in cash or by demand draft at a designated Axis Bank branch, or online, within the time limit.
Take your allotment letter, fee receipt (one term, i.e. 6 months) and original documents to the help centre to confirm admission.
You must have qualified NEET-PG 2026 and be eligible under National Medical Commission rules and Gujarat's admission rules.
Your compulsory rotating internship must be completed on or before 30th September 2026.
MDS isn't part of this notice
The 2026-27 registration advertisement covers MD/MS/Diploma only. Watch medadmgujarat.org for an MDS notice.
Candidates who completed a recognised MBBS from a university established under a law of the Government of Gujarat, located in Gujarat, are eligible.
MBBS outside Gujarat (or not under a Gujarat law), with Gujarat roots

If you did MBBS outside Gujarat, abroad, or at an institution not established under a Gujarat law, you're eligible if you passed 12th (B or AB group) from a school located in Gujarat, under the Gujarat Board, CBSE, CISCE, IB/Cambridge or NIOS, and were born in Gujarat or are domiciled there. The notice words this route for universities established under a Government of India law, so confirm with ACPPGMEC that yours qualifies.
MBBS outside Gujarat (or not under a Gujarat law), without Gujarat schooling and birth/domicile

Candidates who did MBBS outside Gujarat, abroad, or at an institution not established under a Gujarat law don't meet the eligibility criteria unless they did 12th in Gujarat and were born in or are domiciled in Gujarat. If you studied at AIIMS Rajkot, confirm with ACPPGMEC which route applies to you.
NRI quota is still open to you

You don't meet the Government and Management quota criteria, but the NRI quota criteria (p26) don't appear to depend on where you studied. Confirm with ACPPGMEC. You must be an NRI yourself, or your parents must be NRIs. A legal guardian counts only if your parents are absent; while your father is alive, no one else is ordinarily accepted as guardian. Your internship must be completed by 30th September 2026.

NRI follows the Income Tax Act / FEMA definition: a person resident outside India who is an Indian citizen or a Person of Indian Origin (PIO). A PIO is a foreign citizen, not of Pakistan or Bangladesh, who has held an Indian passport, whose parent or grandparent was an Indian citizen, or who is the spouse of an Indian citizen or such a PIO. A second definition in the instructions also counts great-grandparents and excludes other countries the Central Government names; confirm with ACPPGMEC. You count as resident in India if you stayed here more than 182 days in the preceding financial year. This doesn't include someone who left or stays outside India for a job, business or an indefinite stay, or someone who came to or stays in India for a reason other than a job, business or an indefinite stay. You must be an NRI, or your parents must be; a legal guardian counts only if your parents are absent, and while your father is alive no one else is ordinarily accepted as guardian. Pay a ₹25,000 non-refundable processing fee by demand draft. Verification happens only at the ACPPGMEC office, GMERS Medical College, Gandhinagar. Hostel admission isn't guaranteed, hostel fees are set by the college, and other fees are the same as for all students.
The document list asks for proof of Indian citizenship, plus a passport copy if your citizenship is dual or foreign. Foreign and OCI candidates should check whether they qualify under the NRI quota.

Under Rule 4(4), a candidate who secured admission under Gujarat's PG admission rules in any year can't be admitted to any course until that course's duration would have been completed. The registration form asks "Previously Admitted?". The rule doesn't say whether a seat you resigned or never joined counts; confirm with ACPPGMEC.
In-service doctors: 10% of seats in 10 subjects

10% of Government quota seats in MD/MS subjects (Diploma isn't mentioned) in Government and GMERS medical colleges, plus CPS courses in Government hospitals, are for Gujarat in-service doctors. The subjects are Paediatrics, TB & Chest, Obstetrics & Gynaecology, Preventive & Community Medicine, Orthopaedics, General Surgery, General Medicine, Anaesthesiology, Radiology and Pathology. You need an NOC from a Gujarat competent authority.
SC, ST, SEBC and EWS claims need certificates issued by competent authorities of Gujarat State only. Certificates from another state aren't listed as accepted.
PwD: assessment by the ACPUGMEC medical board

PwD applicants must be examined by an ACPUGMEC medical board at one of the listed civil hospitals. Certificates from any other authority or hospital aren't accepted. Under the NMC 2026 guidelines, you need a benchmark disability of at least 40%, a valid UDID card, and notarised Schedule-I affidavits: Appendix-A and Appendix-G for everyone, plus the appendix for your disability type. The certificate is an "Eligibility Certificate" that assesses functional competence, not just disability. Final eligibility is decided only after physical verification and functional assessment. The NMC guidelines are written for MD/MS/DNB, so Diploma candidates should confirm the assessment with ACPPGMEC.
Upload your NBE screening exam (FMGE) marksheet during registration, and verify the original at the help centre.

Your MBBS or FMGE aggregate, as entered in your NEET-PG 2026 form, is verified against your originals at admission. If it was used to break a rank tie and turns out to be wrong, your NEET-PG 2026 candidature is cancelled.
All quotas are filled by the committee
ACPPGMEC fills 100% of MD/MS/Diploma seats in Gujarat, across Government (GQ), Management (MQ) and NRI (NQ) quotas, online and on merit.

SC, ST and SEBC caste certificates, the SEBC non-creamy layer certificate and the EWS certificate must be issued by competent authorities of Gujarat State. Your reservation claim is subject to verification of your caste certificate by the issuing authority.

Non-creamy layer (Parishishta 4) and EWS certificates in Gujarati must be issued on or after 1st April 2024. English certificates must be issued on or after 1st April 2026. Both must be valid for 2026-27.
10% of Government quota seats in 10 MD/MS subjects at Government and GMERS colleges, and CPS courses in Government hospitals, are reserved for Gujarat in-service doctors.
PwD certificate only from ACPUGMEC boards

PwD seats need a certificate from an ACPUGMEC medical board. If the board finds you unfit, you can appeal to the medical appeal board, chaired by the Dean of B. J. Medical College, Ahmedabad, with two experts who weren't on the first board. Appeals about eye-related disabilities go to a board chaired by the Director, M. & J. Institute of Ophthalmology, Ahmedabad. The NMC 2026 guidelines also allow an appeal to a DGHS appellate authority, within the time MCC sets. Confirm which route applies with ACPPGMEC.

Under the NMC 2026 guidelines, the board rates you Eligible, Eligible with reasonable accommodation, or Ineligible for each speciality. For surgical specialities (Anaesthesiology, General Surgery, OBG, Ophthalmology, Orthopaedics, ENT, Traumatology, Emergency Medicine, PMR, Sports Medicine): Upper-limb disability and multiple disabilities are generally not suitable. Speech and language disability is not suitable. Lower-limb disability, and conditions such as cerebral palsy or muscular dystrophy, may be suitable if you show the needed functional competencies. Visual impairment is suitable only if corrective lenses alone bring it below 40%. Hearing impairment is suitable if you function with hearing aids or a cochlear implant and have acceptable, intelligible speech. Mental illness, ASD, SLD and ID are suitable if functional competency is present. Blood disorders are decided case by case. Chronic neurological conditions are suitable if stable, but not with uncontrolled seizures, frequent relapses, progressive neurodegeneration or severe impairment.

A correctable defect in your UDID card alone isn't grounds for denial if your disability is otherwise established. You should have an established diagnosis and a stable condition. Before declaring you ineligible, the board must consider reasonable accommodation and assistive technology. It can't declare you ineligible only because of your diagnosis, disability category or percentage. If you're found ineligible, you must be given a written, reasoned order, and you can appeal.

For other clinical specialities (such as General Medicine, Paediatrics, Dermatology, Psychiatry, Radio-diagnosis and Community Medicine), the NMC 2026 table says: Locomotor disability may be suitable if you show the needed competencies, including optimum use of both upper limbs. Visual impairment is suitable if adaptive devices bring it below 40% while keeping both hands free. Hearing impairment is suitable with hearing aids, an amplified stethoscope or a cochlear implant, if your speech is acceptable and intelligible. Speech and language disability is suitable if your speech is intelligible. Mental illness, ASD, SLD and ID are suitable if functional competency is present. Blood disorders are suitable. Chronic neurological conditions are suitable if stable, but not with uncontrolled seizures, frequent relapses, progressive neurodegeneration or severe impairment. Multiple disabilities are suitable with functional adequacy.

For Anatomy, Physiology, Biochemistry and Biophysics, the NMC 2026 table says: Locomotor disability is suitable, with ramps and adjustable tables. Visual impairment is suitable if a low vision aid brings it below 40%. Hearing impairment is suitable with hearing aids or a cochlear implant, if your speech is acceptable and intelligible. Speech disability is not suitable. Mental illness, ASD, SLD and ID are suitable if functional competency is present. Blood disorders and chronic neurological conditions are suitable. Multiple disabilities are suitable if you're functional.

For Pharmacology, Pathology, Microbiology, and Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, the NMC 2026 table says: Locomotor disability is suitable, with modified labs and mobility aids. Visual impairment is suitable if digital aids bring it below 40%. Hearing impairment is suitable with hearing aids or a cochlear implant, if your speech is acceptable and intelligible. Speech disability is suitable. Mental illness, ASD, SLD and ID are suitable if stable. Blood disorders and chronic neurological conditions are suitable. Multiple disabilities are suitable with competence.
Paid with the PIN on medadmgujarat.org (₹28,000 total with the deposit). The 2026 documents don't say whether later rounds need fresh registration.
NRI applicants also pay a ₹25,000 non-refundable processing fee by demand draft in favour of “ACPUGMEC”, payable at Gandhinagar, at the ACPPGMEC office.
NRI fees are in US$ and non-refundable

The NRI student and their parent or legal guardian sign a notarised undertaking to pay the college's NRI fee in US$ for the entire course. It isn't negotiable or refundable except as the admission rules allow. Extra fees apply each term if study runs beyond the normal period plus one year of internship (as the form words it); confirm how this applies to PG with the college. If dues aren't cleared, the student may not be sent up for exams.
Keep your PIN until admission and refunds are over. To regenerate a lost PIN, visit CCR, GMERS Medical College, Gandhinagar and pay ₹500.
Pay tuition by cash or DD at a designated Axis Bank branch, or online, within the deadline. For admission you need a receipt for one term (6 months) of fees.
After the merit list, choice filling opens online for each round. Allotments are published after the window closes.
Check your merit number and category
Make sure the merit number and category on the merit list match your registration details.
Don't share your PIN or password. Store your ID, password and PIN in several places, not only on your phone.
NRI seats are allotted on inter-se merit by NEET-PG All India Overall Rank among the candidates who applied for NRI seats.
See your allotment in your login
Allotment status is shown on the website. Log in with your user ID to see yours.
From Round 1, help centres verify only original documents. DigiLocker documents and colour photocopies or printouts aren't accepted. Bring originals plus one self-attested photocopy set.
Online registration alone isn't enough. Without verification at a help centre and a stamped registration slip, you can't continue in the admission process.
All admission information is published only on the admission committee website. Check it often.

NRI applications aren't considered without notarised copies of the certificates. Report any change to your documents or marks promptly to the ACPPGMEC office. If any discrepancy is found, the admission is liable to be cancelled, the candidate could be expelled, and criminal action would be initiated. The Chairman, ACPPGMEC can change these guidelines, and his interpretation is final.
Printed registration details, signed by you and a parent or guardian
All MBBS marksheets, year- and attempt-wise
Internship completion certificate (on or before 30th September 2026)
Provisional State Medical Council registration (if you just completed internship) or permanent Medical Council / MCI registration (earlier pass-outs)

Proof of your date and place of birth and Indian citizenship. The school leaving or transfer certificate is compulsory for everyone. Add a birth certificate or passport if your place of birth isn't on it.
Caste certificate from a Gujarat competent authority
Non-creamy layer certificate (Parishishta 4) from a Gujarat competent authority
Gujarati: issued on or after 1st April 2024. English: issued on or after 1st April 2026. Valid for 2026-27.
EWS certificate from a Gujarat competent authority
Gujarati: issued on or after 1st April 2024. English: issued on or after 1st April 2026. Valid for 2026-27.
Disability certificate from an ACPUGMEC medical board
Issued through the UDID portal (Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment). The medical board verifies it.

All PwBD applicants submit notarised Appendix-A (general self-certification) and Appendix-G (mandatory; you declare you understand your chosen speciality's demands and will perform its tasks). Depending on your disability, also submit Appendix-B (hearing), C (upper limb), D (lower limb), E (mental illness, speech disorders, specific learning disorder or autism) or F (visual). For Appendix-F, your low vision aid must bring your visual disability below 40%, give a field of vision over 40 degrees, and be hands-free. Other disabilities, such as blood disorders or chronic neurological conditions, need Appendix-A only (plus G). In the affidavits you name the PG courses you intend to pursue. A false declaration may cost you your admission.
For candidates who did MBBS outside Gujarat.
For candidates who did MBBS outside Gujarat and were born outside Gujarat.
No Objection Certificate from a Gujarat competent authority

₹25,000 demand draft, plus notarised copies of: printout of the online application, all MBBS marksheets, NEET-PG marksheet, school leaving certificate and 12th marksheet. Notarised colour copies of: passport (all pages, including blank ones) of you or your NRI parent; visa, residence permit or OCI/PIO card; NRI certificate from the Indian Embassy, High Commission or Consulate; Indian and foreign address proof; fee undertaking on ₹300 stamp paper (notarised); proof of origin. Bring the originals and notarised colour copies when you submit the application, and all documents to the interview. Also fill in the stay-in-India form for 1st April 2025 to 31st March 2026: each arrival and departure date with its passport page number, days per stay and total days, signed by you and your parent. Documents not in English must be translated by a competent authority.
Photocopy of your disability certificate (at admission)
Authority letter (only if a family member verifies on your behalf)

Only a mother, father, grandparent, brother, sister or guardian can act for you. Attach recent passport photos of you and the authority holder. The letter is signed by you and a parent, and the holder brings original and photocopy ID (driving licence, PAN, passport, election card or Aadhaar).
Help centres: 10:00 AM–4:00 PM; Saturday 10:00 AM–12:00 noon; closed Sundays and government holidays
For any guidance on registration or later steps, visit your nearest help centre.

Speciality-wise functional assessment for PwBD candidates. The minimum benchmark disability is 40%. The medical board issues an Eligibility Certificate: Eligible, Eligible with reasonable accommodation (naming it), or Ineligible (with reasons).
